name: অগ্নীশ্বরর মন্দির, তিরুপ্পুগলুর
deity: অগ্নীশ্বরর (অগ্নিপুরীশ্বরর) রূপে শিব, দেবী করুন্দার্কুড়লি-র সঙ্গে
period: তেবারম যুগ (৭ম শতাব্দীতে গীত); বর্তমান চোল কাঠামোগত মন্দির, আনু. ১০ম শতাব্দী
summary: তিরুপ্পুগলুর, নাগপট্টিনমের নিম্ন কাবেরী বদ্বীপে, শিবকে অগ্নীশ্বরর রূপে — অগ্নিপুরীশ্বরর — দেবী করুন্দার্কুড়লির সঙ্গে সম্মান করে। অপ্পর, সম্বন্দর ও সুন্দরর কর্তৃক গীত একটি পাডল পেট্র স্থলম্, এর নাম অগ্নিদেবের তপস্যার সঙ্গে জড়িত, যাঁর তীর্থকুণ্ড, অগ্নি তীর্থম, এখনও মন্দিরকে ঘিরে আছে।

sections.history: Tiruppugalur lies in Nagapattinam district, in the lower Kaveri delta. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Appar (Tirunavukkarasar), Sambandar and Sundarar, counted among the Shiva shrines on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The present stone temple is of the Chola period, about the 10th century. The complex holds two Paadal Petra shrines — Agneeswarar and Vardhamaneswarar.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Agneeswarar — Agnipureeswarar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Karundharkuzhali (also Choolikambal) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. A water body, the Agni Theertham, encircles the shrine. The walled courtyard keeps the form of the Shiva temples of the lower Nagapattinam delta, and the shrine of Vardhamaneswarar stands within the same sacred ground.
sections.legends: Shiva is worshipped here as Agneeswarar, 'the lord of Agni,' for Agni, the fire-god, is said to have done penance at this place and raised a body of water around himself; that tank survives to this day as the Agni Theertham, and the lord's name recalls the fire-god's worship. The goddess is Karundharkuzhali. As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims of the lower Nagapattinam delta include Tiruppugalur among their stops, worshipping at both of its Paadal Petra shrines.
sections.experience: At Tiruppugalur the pilgrim comes to the lord of the fire-god's penance. Before Agneeswarar and Karundharkuzhali, with the Agni Theertham encircling the shrine, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple of the lower delta, firm in the memory of Agni's worship.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruppugalur lies in Nagapattinam district, in the lower Kaveri delta. Nagapattinam and Tiruvarur are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
